harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and applied the transactional SQLite v1-to-v2 migration on node1. The catalog retained IDs and descriptions, gained a nonnegative price_cents field initialized to zero, remains repeat-safe, and recovered successfully after reboot without changing the OS release or kernel.
actions_performed: Replaced bin/upgrade.py with an atomic SQLite migration that updates schema_version last and rolls back on errors.
Validated rollback using an injected final-step failure against an isolated v1 database.
Ran the migration repeatedly against isolated and live databases.
Verified database integrity, preserved products, zero-valued prices, and rejection of negative prices.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Migration is transactional and leaves v1 usable upon failure
evidence.summary: An injected schema-version update failure rolled back the added column; schema_version remained 1, original products remained readable, and integrity_check was ok.

evidence.requirement: Existing IDs/descriptions retained and price_cents added with zero default and nonnegative constraint
evidence.summary: Original rows 1/Paper and 2/Tape became 1/Paper/0 and 2/Tape/0. The live schema includes NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(price_cents >= 0), and a negative insert was rejected.

evidence.requirement: schema_version advances only after successful upgrade and migration is repeat-safe
evidence.summary: The final-step failure preserved version 1, while two consecutive successful live executions produced and retained version 2 with integrity_check=ok.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux 6.8.0-71-generic were retained through the work and reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45 was captured, reboot was acknowledged, new boot ID 579b06c0-9e51-4f20-bbbc-4cd4395cc2e4 was observed, and system, migration file, schema v2, integrity, and product data recovered.
